recipe.history: Cranberries are one of the few foods native to North America, a tart, scarlet fruit that grew wild in the acidic bogs of New England and the Great Lakes long before European contact. The Wampanoag and other Algonquian peoples called them by names that translated roughly as "bitter berry" and used them medicinally, mixed with fat and dried venison as a preservation technique, and crushed them with maple sugar as a relish. When the Pilgrims arrived at Plymouth, they encountered cranberries already woven into Indigenous foodways, and by the 17th century, colonists were boiling them with sugar into a sauce that could stand alongside roasted game. The cranberry's natural pectin made it an ideal candidate for sauce and jelly, and its ability to grow in flooded bogs that were otherwise agriculturally useless made it a New England staple. By the 19th century, Ocean Spray and other cooperatives had industrialized the cranberry harvest, and the canned jellied cylinder of cranberry sauce became one of the most iconic and ironically beloved features of the American Thanksgiving table.
ingredients: 180g (¾ cup / 1½ sticks) unsalted butter, softened and cubed
1 egg beaten with 1 tbsp cream (egg wash)
4 thick slices day-old white sandwich bread, cut into ½-inch cubes
Kosher salt and black pepper to taste
120ml (½ cup) low-sodium turkey or chicken broth
Kosher salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: 1. MAKE THE BRIOCHE BUNS — In a stand mixer with the dough hook, combine flour, yeast, sugar, and salt. Whisk briefly.
2. Add eggs and warm milk. Mix on low until a rough dough forms, about 3 minutes.
3. Knead on medium speed for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
4. With the mixer running on medium-low, add butter a few cubes at a time, waiting until each addition is fully incorporated before adding more. This process takes 8–10 minutes.
5. Increase speed to medium and knead 5 more minutes until the dough is very smooth and pulls away from the bowl sides. It will be soft and slightly tacky.
6. Transfer dough to a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate overnight (8–12 hours). Cold fermentation develops flavor and makes the dough easier to shape.

7. The next day, remove the dough and divide into 4 equal portions. Shape into tight round balls. Place on a parchment-lined sheet pan, flatten slightly, cover, and proof at room temperature for 2–3 hours until doubled and puffy.
8. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Brush with egg wash. Bake 18–20 minutes until deep golden brown. Cool completely on a wire rack.
9. MAKE THE CRANBERRY SAUCE — Combine cranberries, sugar, orange juice, orange zest, and salt in a small saucepan over medium heat.
10. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the cranberries burst and the mixture thickens to a jam-like consistency, 10–12 minutes. Let cool. It will thicken further as it cools.
11. MAKE THE STUFFING CROUTONS — Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Spread bread cubes on a baking sheet and toast 10–12 minutes until lightly crisp. Set aside.
12. Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add onion and celery; cook until softened, 5 minutes.
13. Add sage and thyme; cook 1 minute. Add the toasted bread cubes and toss to coat.
14. Pour in the chicken broth and stir until the bread absorbs the liquid and the mixture clumps slightly but still has some crisp bits. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
15. MAKE THE GRAVY AIOLI — Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook 1 minute until lightly golden.
16. Slowly whisk in the broth and cook, whisking constantly, until thickened into a smooth gravy, 3–4 minutes. Add thyme. Season with salt and pepper. Let cool to room temperature.
17. Stir the cooled gravy into the mayonnaise along with the whole grain mustard until smooth. Adjust seasoning. Refrigerate until ready to use.

18. FORM THE PATTIES — Combine ground beef, ground turkey, salt, pepper, sage, thyme, rosemary, garlic powder, and Worcestershire sauce in a bowl. Mix gently with your hands until just combined — do not overwork.
19. Divide into 4 equal portions (about 170g each). Form into patties about ¾-inch thick with a thumb dimple in the center.
20. COOK THE PATTIES — Heat a cast-iron skillet over high heat with a thin film of neutral oil until smoking.
21. Cook patties undisturbed for 3–3½ minutes until a deep brown crust forms. Flip once.

22. Cook 2½–3 minutes more. The turkey component means a slightly longer cook, but the beef blend means medium rare (130–135°F / 54–57°C) is still the target — the fat from the 80/20 beef keeps moisture in. Check with an instant-read thermometer.
23. Remove from heat and rest under foil for 3 minutes.
24. TOAST THE BUNS — Split brioche buns and toast cut-side down in the residual fat in the pan until golden, 60 seconds.
25. ASSEMBLE — Spread gravy aioli on both cut sides of each bun.
26. Place a romaine leaf on the bottom bun. Set the patty on top.
27. Spoon a generous tablespoon of cranberry sauce over the patty.
28. Top with a heaping spoonful of stuffing croutons.
29. Close with the top bun and serve immediately — this is Thanksgiving on a bun.
